topics.title: Qantas tests an ultra-long-range Airbus
topics.summary: A Qantas Airbus A350-1000ULR completed a nonstop 17,000-kilometre test flight from Toulouse to Melbourne in just over 19 hours. The aircraft is being prepared for future direct routes between Sydney and London.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would skipping a connection make a 20-hour flight sound appealing, or would you rather break the trip up? What would make that much time onboard comfortable?

topics.title: Most English riverbanks remain out of reach
topics.summary: New analysis from the Right to Roam campaign says 71% of riverbanks across 89 English catchments lack nearby public access. Campaigners want broader responsible access as hot weather increases interest in walking, paddling and swimming.
topics.discussionPrompt: Should rivers and their banks be treated more like public spaces, or should access depend on who owns the land? What would responsible access look like?

topics.title: Community forestry creates green islands in Guatemala
topics.summary: Community-run forestry concessions in Guatemala’s Maya biosphere reserve have maintained near-zero deforestation while supporting local jobs. Strict harvesting rotations, tree mapping and nurseries let residents earn from the forest while helping it recover.
topics.discussionPrompt: Can carefully managed logging actually help protect a forest better than banning all use? What local rules would make you trust a conservation project?

topics.title: Netflix looks beyond the binge-watch era
topics.summary: Netflix is adapting as audience growth slows and viewers divide their time among streaming rivals, YouTube and social platforms. Its next phase may depend on live programming, advertising and giving individual shows more room to become shared events.
topics.discussionPrompt: Do you prefer getting a whole season at once or waiting for weekly episodes? Which approach makes a show more fun to talk about with other people?
